If we are inserting a SQL NULL we will get actual NULL back, our JSON processing is somehow turning `null` to `'null'`. If we fix that this problem will not appear
Why this need special treatment for MySQL, it seems to work with Postgres and SQLite ?

It's not the sequelize JSON processing that is returning `'null'` as a string. Let's say we have the following JSON data:
```json
{ "test": null }
```

In that case, MySQL returns `'null'` as a string when we run the following query:
```sql
SELECT data->>'$.test' FROM table
```

MySQL only returns NULL when the property doesn't exist in the JSON document.
I'm thinking about using the [JSON_TYPE function](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/json-attribute-functions.html#function_json-type) because, in that case, it returns `'NULL'` (rather than `'STRING'`).
So the final query would be something similiar to this:
```sql
SELECT * FROM table WHERE (data->>'$.test' IS NULL OR JSON_TYPE(data->>'$.test') = 'NULL')
```
